rationale: C23 plausibly supplied a concrete and material drafting template for the child's registration provisions. The child adapts C23's sequence and language for a new class of special registrants: duty to register, registration after separation from a reserve component, registration after entering the United States, registration upon leaving an institution, and responsibility for performing the duty. C12 and C03 also materially underlie later portions concerning classification and physical examination, but C23 provides the clearest sustained language-and-structure match.

shared_material.child_excerpt: § 1650.3 Duty to be registered. (a) On the day or days and between the hours fixed by proclamation of the President or order of the Director of Selective Service ... every person required to do so ... shall present himself for and submit to registration before a duly designated registration official or the local board having jurisdiction in the area in which he has a permanent home or in which he may happen to be on that day or any of those days.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: § 611.1 Duty to be registered. ... On the day or days and between the hours fixed for registration by Presidential proclamation, every man required to do so ... shall present himself for and submit to registration before a duly designated registration official or the local board having jurisdiction in the area in which he has his permanent home or in which he may happen to be on that day or any of those days.
shared_material.explanation: Near-verbatim operative language adapted to permit special registrations ordered by either the President or the Director.

shared_material.child_excerpt: § 1650.4 Registration of persons separated from reserve components of the armed forces. Every male person who ... would have been required to register ... except for the fact that he was a member of a reserve component ... is thereafter separated ... and ... has not been registered ... shall present himself for and submit to registration before a local board within the period of thirty days following the date on which he was so separated.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: § 611.3 Registration of men separated from armed forces. Every man who (a) has been separated from active service in the armed forces ... (b) has not been registered prior to such separation, and (c) would have been required to be registered except for the fact that he was in such active service ... shall present himself for and submit to registration before a local board within the period of 30 day following the date on which he was so separated.
shared_material.explanation: The child reuses the same three-condition rule and thirty-day registration deadline, changing the exempting status to membership in a reserve component.

shared_material.child_excerpt: § 1650.5 Registration of certain persons entering the United States. Every male person who would have been required to register ... had he been within the United States and who thereafter enters the United States shall present himself for and submit to registration before a local board within the period of five days following the date on which he enters the United States.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: § 611.4 Registration of certain persons entering the United States. (a) Every male person who would have been required to register ... had he been within the United States and who thereafter enters the United States shall present himself for and submit to registration before a local board within the period of five days following the date on which he enters the United States.
shared_material.explanation: This is essentially verbatim reuse of a complete operative provision.

shared_material.child_excerpt: § 1650.6 Inmate of institution. Unless he has already been registered, every person subject to registration in any special registration ... who is an inmate of an insane asylum, jail, penitentiary, reformatory, or similar institution shall be registered on the day he leaves the institution.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: § 611.5 Inmate of institution. Unless he has already been registered, every person subject to registration who is an inmate of an insane asylum, jail, penitentiary, reformatory, or similar institution shall be registered on the day he leaves the institution.
shared_material.explanation: Verbatim provision with only the special-registration limitation inserted.
